notes: The brief is missing the biggest incident of the last 24 hours: UKMTO reported a tanker struck by multiple projectiles about 51 nautical miles north of Madinat ash Shamal, Qatar, at about 1900 UTC on 7 October, with casualties. It is held as INC-20261007-003 but was wrongly merged into the 5 October On Peace record, so restore it as its own Gulf item and keep Oman's On Peace evacuation in a separate paragraph.

The Alfa Watan's crew are missing, not killed: Bulgaria called off the search on 7 October with no trace of the sailors, and the number aboard is disputed (Maritime.bg said ten, Bulgaria's rescue chief said twelve, all Syrian). Say ten or twelve crew missing and feared dead, never ten killed.

The headline, standfirst and lede treat the Alfa Watan as a 7 October attack; it sank on 6 October and was covered yesterday, so rebuild the lead around the 7 October Qatar tanker strike. What crews should know must not list Sochi and the Strait of Hormuz once those duplicated items are removed; say the day's incidents were the tanker hit off Qatar and the shots at the CUL Klang in the southern Red Sea.
The containership fired on in the southern Red Sea is the Singapore-flagged CUL Klang, operated by Chinese CUL Lines, so say Singapore-flagged and name the ship, not a Chinese containership.

The Qatar tanker strike (UKMTO, 7 October, about 1900 UTC, casualties) is now its own incident in the facts and leads the brief. The Gulf is not quiet today: never say no new attacks were reported in the Strait of Hormuz and the Gulf. This replaces the earlier On Peace note: do not mention Oman's On Peace at all today.

What crews should know: only report any attack or suspicious approach to UKMTO, and follow UKMTO and JMIC advisories and company security instructions. No statistics or counts in that section; the seven-day count belongs once in the second paragraph.
